items.text: README excerpt for AskDocs, the internal document Q&A bot at Larkspur & Vale. The assistant ingests PDFs and Slack exports, then answers questions with citations back to the source paragraph. Setup instructions are in docs/setup.md; run `make index` after dropping files into the corpus folder. Note that OCR quality varies a lot on scanned invoices, so the assistant sometimes misreads amounts — treat those answers as a starting point, not gospel. If you change the chunking rules in config.yaml, re-run the evaluation suite before opening a PR.

Onboarding checklist for new hires on the support team (week one). Before day one, IT sends the welcome email with a temporary password for the ticketing system; the new hire must change it at first login. Someone from People Ops walks them through the building rules around badge access and fire drills, which is honestly the most boring forty minutes of the week.

Day two is shadowing. The new hire sits with a senior agent and listens to calls, then tries a few themselves with the senior listening in. We point them at the internal document assistant so they can search the policy wiki by question instead of scrolling, but remind them the assistant only quotes what's in the wiki — if a policy looks out of date, escalate to the policy owner rather than trusting the answer.

The rest of the week covers the refund tooling, the escalation matrix, and a short quiz on data-handling rules. Managers should sign off on the checklist by Friday afternoon. If anything in the checklist doesn't match what actually happens on the floor, tell Priya in #support-ops so we can fix the doc.

Internal note for the parcel-tracking assistant, v0.9. The chatbot pulls status from the Halcyon Couriers API every ten minutes and answers 'where is my parcel' questions in plain English. When a parcel is marked lost, the assistant should point customers at the claims form and quote the 28-day window from the shipping terms. Please keep the language warm — people asking about lost parcels are usually stressed. The tone guidelines live in docs/voice.md and override the defaults baked into the model.

# retriever.py
# Wraps the embedding client and the vector store. The document assistant
# calls `search()` with the user's question and gets back the top-k chunks.
# Performance note: batch the embed calls, otherwise indexing a 200-page
# wedding binder takes forever. We also strip boilerplate headers before
# embedding, since they pollute the similarity scores.

def search(question: str, k: int = 6) -> list[Chunk]:
    vectors = embed([question])
    return store.query(vectors, top_k=k)

A note on how we built the lost-parcel FAQ for the help centre. We tested a few phrasings with the support chatbot and kept the ones where customers actually clicked through to the claims page. The security team asked us to strip the tracking numbers from the sample screenshots, since a tracking number is almost as sensitive as a password. Legal also wanted the word 'compensation' removed from the headings, because it overpromised. Current draft is in the shared drive under Help/Shipping/FAQ-v3.docx.

The wedding assistant has one job: answer guest questions about the schedule using the couple's shared folder. It should never invent details about the venue or the dress code, and it should quote the couple's own words where possible. When guests ask about gifts, the assistant links the registry page and nothing else. The couple review the folder monthly, so stale answers are usually our fault, not the model's.

Onboarding checklist — contractors, facilities team. Contractors get a temporary badge and a one-time password for the work-order portal. Their manager confirms the portal access request before IT provisions anything. The facilities chatbot can answer questions about loading-dock rules and recycling schedules, which cuts down on repetitive Slack pings. Any contractor who needs after-hours access must have it approved in writing by the building manager, and the request goes in the portal, not over email.
